acceptance: The workflow_run trigger carries a branches filter for chore/sqlglot-* (kept consistent with the delivery trust root's branchPrefix, as the existing drift test does for the arm job if).
A non-adoption CI or review completion starts no run of this workflow.
An adoption PR's CI and review completions still trigger the arm job, shown by the workflow contract tests.
context:
Decision gate: none needed for the trigger filter. If the branches filter cannot express the trust root's branchPrefix exactly, stop and ask the owner before changing the arm job's condition.

Verification rubric: (1) workflow contract tests, including the branchPrefix drift test, extended to the new branches filter, fail before and pass after; (2) actionlint shows no new findings (the existing queue and SC2086 findings are pre-existing); (3) confirm from GitHub's docs that workflow_run branches filters on the triggering run's head branch; (4) after merge, record the delivery run count for 24 hours before and after: non-adoption CI and review completions start no run, and a dry-run dispatch still passes readiness with state current.

Guardrails: schedule and workflow_dispatch triggers, the readiness, prepare and publish jobs, and the arm job's if stay unchanged; no new permission or secret; ship through the core PR flow (make worktree-create, make pr-preflight, make pr-open, make pr-arm) with a changelog fragment marked internal.
description: sqlglot-delivery.yml triggers on workflow_run completion of CI, review-verdict and review-gate with no branches filter; the arm job's if (startsWith(head_branch, 'chore/sqlglot-')) is the only scope. The workflow therefore starts a run for every such completion in the repository: 780 runs between 2026-11-11T15:00Z and 2026-11-12T15:00Z, all skipped. The 200 most recent runs were all skipped workflow_run runs, which buried the scheduled and dispatched runs (finding the four 2026-11-11 dispatch startup_failures needed --event filters), and each run enters the workflow-level concurrency group sqlglot-delivery (queue: max) ahead of or behind real schedule and dispatch runs. Introduced with event-driven arming in #4075.
